name: Eliahba
overview: Eliahba was a male warrior known as the Shaalbonite and recognized as the twenty-second member of "the thirty," a distinguished group of David's mighty men. The biblical record specifically highlights his inclusion among these elite soldiers who served King David. There is no additional tribal or personal information provided about him beyond his military status.
namesAndTitles: The name Eliahba means "G-d hides," reflecting a Hebrew origin that emphasizes divine protection or concealment. This proper name, as recorded in 2 Samuel 23:32, does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries a meaningful theological implication consistent with the faith context of David's warriors.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture infers that Eliahba was the son of Jashen and also the son of Jonathan, as noted in 2 Samuel 23:32. These relationships provide limited genealogical insight but establish a familial background linked to his identity. Beyond these inferred paternal connections, no further family details are recorded.
scriptureSignificance: Eliahba's significance lies primarily in his role as one of David's mighty men, a select group of warriors who were instrumental in establishing and securing David's kingdom. His designation as the twenty-second of "the thirty" highlights his valor and trusted position within this elite band. This association underscores the biblical theme of God raising faithful men to accomplish His purposes through leadership and military strength.
